9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that previously in respect of the disputed property there was another Civil Revision being No. 3800 of 2007 in this court invoking the provisions laid down in section 115(1) of, the Code of Civil Procedure and in that Civil Revision the Rule was made absolute with an order of remand to the appellate court for passing a fresh judgment after rectification and compliance of a direction. For proving the genuineness of the plaintiffs claim of settlement from the government and for proper adjudication into the matter of -controversy the group settlement case record was called for as per direction of this Court. After getting partial of that case record; the lower appellate court found the existence of the Group settlement case. Following the direction of this court on an application from the side of the plaintiffs the court of appeal called for the original record/volume from the offices of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion as well as A.D.C. (Rev.), Bhola.' It has come to the notice of this court that after getting the order of the Court partial original papers were sent without sending the case record as a whole and the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion, Bhola sent the Roll of K.M. settlement, wherefrom it is apparent that a Group Settlement Case No. 157-F/1950-51 was started and the page of said settlement-roll go to show that there are four settlement holders whose serial numbers are 23,24,25 and 26. In serial No. 24 there is an inclusion of plaintiffs predecessor's name viz. Abdul Mannan Mijhi, son of Arfan Ali Mijhi. Against the name of that Abdul Mannan it has been clearly mentioned that the disputed land of schedule cka' measuring an area of 00810 `Shahasrangsa' in plot No. 4205/6 under the government khash khatian has been settled by the government in the year 1-957 in favour of Abdul Mannan Mijhi and the amount of Salami was fixed against the suit land. It is to be noted here that the land included within this paper marked as Exhibit-1 and in respect of the land of the government khash khatian 04(four) persons having serial No. 23-26 obtained settlement pursuant to a K.M. settlement roll and therefore it is clear that the said settlement of the government is nothing but a group settlement as contended by the plaintiffs. Apart from this; it is obvious to note that the concerned tahshilder pursuant to that settlement granted receipts in favour of the' plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan after acceptance of selami against the disputed property. In the year 1998 also the concerned official after acceptance of rent granted receipts in favour of plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest vide Exhibits No.2 and 2(ka). 

 10. In this context; having gone through the impugned judgment and decree I find that the learned appellate court below scanning the said papers conclusively held that on perusal of the certified copy of K.M. settlement case marked as exhibit- l along with two D.C.Rs. it appears that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan in Group Settlement Case No.157-F/1950-51 in serial No.24 obtained the suit land and accordingly paid selami in favour of the government. It is also held by the lower appellate court that the claim of the plaintiffs appears to be correct. Subsequent to that; the learned court below holding the view that inasmuch as the settlement was not completed and no khatian was opened neither in the name of the settlement holder nor in the names of the plaintiffs; the plaintiffs are not entitled to get the relief as prayed for. It is the observation of the appellate court in the concluding portion of the impugned judgment that:বাদী পক্ষের পূববর্তী আঃ মান্নানের নামে নাঃ ভূমি বাবদ  ১৫৭/৫০-৫১ নং গ্রুপ সেটেলমেন্ট কেস রজু থাকায় উযধশক্ত বন্দোবস্তের বিষয়টি চুড়ান্ত করার নিমিত্তে আবশ্যকীয় প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা যুক্তে বাদী পক্ষের আদালতের স্নরনাপন্ন হওয়া যুক্তিযুক্ত ও সংগত ছিল। From the aforesaid recital of the impugned judgment and decree it is evident that the lower appellate court awarded no decree in favour of the plaintiffs inasmuch as the appropriate relief was not sought for. 

 11. From the discussions spelt out earlier it is apparent that the learned lower appellate court is totally misconceived in appreciating the actual position of law and has failed to evaluate the evidence on records in its total approach. The findings suffer from contradiction and proper appreciation of the evidence on records. The fact remains that the government admits that the suit land was settled with the plaintiffs predecessor by group settlement case and accordingly K.M. settlement was done. In the said Settlement Case No.157-F/1950-51 four persons including the predecessor of the plaintiffs obtained settlement and the selami which was fixed including the rents therein has been duly accepted by the government after granting receipts. As such; it cannot be held that the plaintiffs predecessor had any malafide intention or that the plaintiffs case suffers from suppression of facts rather it is evident that it is the bonafide claim of the plaintiffs in respect of the disputed property and they possess the same from the settlement of their predecessor-in-interest since 1957. The subsequent act of filing the miscellaneous case by the defendant No.3 Assistant Commissioner (Land), Charfashion, Bhola cannot be treated as legal.
